fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Around a Customer Story
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the story page, the request form under it, and the table where every buyer who asks for a demo is kept.
fields.feature_1:
A full story from one paragraph

Paste the customer's name, the problem, and the result, and Emergent builds the page: headline number, challenge, approach, and quote. Change any section with a prompt.
fields.feature_2:
The result where buyers look first

Prompt for the headline figure, such as hours saved or cost cut, in a band above the story. A buyer who reads only the top of the page still leaves knowing the number.
fields.feature_3:
Demo requests tagged with the story

The app saves each request to a database you own, with the buyer's company and the story they read. With several stories live, the table shows which result brings in buyers.
fields.feature_4:
The right person hears about it

Name who should be told in your prompt, such as the account owner or the rep who shared the link, and the app sends them an email, Slack, or in-app alert with the request.
fields.feature_5:
Requests that land in your CRM

The app connects to any tool with an API, HubSpot among them. A request from the story page can arrive in the CRM as a contact with the case study name on it, never retyped.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Publish the case study on a custom domain such as yours.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans add full code export to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Anouk Verhaegen's link led May with 19 opens

Quillwater's story on Sabledge Freight goes out through 5 sales reps, each with a link of their own. When a prospect opens a rep's link, the app emails that rep. In May the links were opened 47 times, and 19 of those opens came from Anouk Verhaegen's link.
fields.tab_content_2:
Visitors who pick dental see that story first

Northvane IT's case study page first asks a visitor's industry: dental, law firm, or manufacturing. A visitor who picks dental reads the dental story first, and each consult request is saved with the industry picked. Of April's 58 requests, 27 came from dental, 19 from law firms, and 12 from manufacturing.
fields.tab_content_3:
$1,240 per compressor becomes each visitor's estimate

Thistledown Creamery saves $1,240 a month per compressor since Varrick Air Systems refit them. A calculator under the story asks how many compressors a visitor runs and multiplies by $1,240. Wexford Bakeries entered 6 and saw estimated savings of $7,440 a month, saved with its demo request.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three quotes approved, one waiting on an edit

Before the page goes live, Grafton Analytics sends its draft case study to Tove Ferrante at Ebbsfleet Clinics. She approves each of the 4 quotes or asks for an edit, and the page stays a draft until all 4 are approved. So far 3 of the 4 quotes are approved and 1 has an edit request: she wants the patient count rounded.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Case Study Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a case study landing page from one customer result to a live page that routes each demo request.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick a result you can count
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put the number in the headline
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a customer whose outcome has a number in it: hours saved a week, cost cut a month, or days taken off onboarding. A buyer can repeat a number to their team; an adjective gets forgotten.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send the draft quotes and figures to your contact at the customer before you build anything. Agree up front which details stay out, such as their prices or headcount. Pulling a figure after launch costs more goodwill than leaving it out.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Lead with the result in the customer's own unit, such as 9 hours a week back for the dispatch team. The detail sits under it for readers who want to see how the result came about.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell what was broken before, then what changed, in a short paragraph each. Give the customer's quote a line of its own, and cut any sentence that a competitor could also say about itself.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the story into Emergent along with the action you want under it, such as a demo request or a consult form. Emergent builds both, with a table behind the form that keeps every request.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Name who hears about each request
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give every request one owner and name that person in the prompt. A buyer who asks to talk should hear back from someone who already knows the account, within the same working day.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test request, confirm the row lands in your table and the alert reaches the right person, then publish the page on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits) and share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a case study landing page?
faq_plan.a: A case study landing page is a single page that tells one customer's story to buyers who are still deciding. It names the customer, leads with the result they got, explains what changed, and ends with one next step, such as a demo request. Unlike a case study in a blog or a resources library, it stands alone: a sales rep can send the link, and an ad can point straight to it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a case study landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the story and the action you want in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder, and Emergent builds the page and its request form, plus the database the requests go into. Before you start, gather the result with its number and a customer quote, and get the customer's approval. Then test a request and publish.

faq_plan.q: What do good case study landing page examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: Good case study landing page examples put a number at the top that a buyer could repeat in a meeting, such as two days cut from every month-end close. They also name a real customer, and when the logo is allowed, they show it. Each one ends with a single action placed right after the result, instead of a menu of links that leads the buyer away from the story.

faq_plan.q: Should landing page case studies be gated behind a form?
faq_plan.a: Gate only the long version. A short story that builds trust works best open, with the request form placed after the result, because a buyer has to read it before they want to talk. A full report with method and data can sit behind a form, offered the way a lead magnet landing page offers a guide in exchange for an email.

faq_plan.q: What sections should a case study landing page include?
faq_plan.a: Include five: a headline with the result, a short note on the customer and who they are, the problem they had before, what changed, and the next step for the reader. Add the customer's quote between the problem and the change, where it reads as proof. Emergent builds these sections from a plain-English prompt, and you change any of them by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: How many words should a case study landing page run?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 400 to 800 words: one screen for the result, then a few short paragraphs of story. A buyer skimming the page should get the outcome from the headline alone, and a buyer who reads on should find the detail in under five minutes. Cut background the customer would not tell a peer over coffee.

faq_plan.q: What call to action works best on a case study landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the next sales step: a demo or a short call with the team that did the work. The story does the proving; the action asks for the conversation it earns. A request to download something belongs on an ebook landing page, where the content itself is the offer, and works against a story page by sending the buyer away to read.

faq_plan.q: How do I get a customer to approve a case study landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ask right after a win they would want to talk about, such as a renewal or a project that hit its goal. Offer to write the draft yourself so it costs them an hour of review, not a day of writing. Tell them up front that they approve every quote and number before anything goes live, and that they can keep details like prices out.

faq_plan.q: How can I tell which landing page case study leads to sales?
faq_plan.a: Tag every request with the story it came from, then follow those requests through to closed deals in your CRM. One hidden field on the form does it: the page fills in the story name, and the buyer never sees it. Apps built on Emergent can sync each request out to HubSpot with that tag, while the requests themselves stay in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: When does ad traffic belong on a case study landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ad traffic belongs there when the ad reaches buyers who already know the problem and want proof that it can be solved. Match the ad to one story and one result, and send the visitor straight to that page. For a broader offer with several messages in rotation, a campaign landing page fits better, and the case study can be linked from there.

plan.angle: Searchers for a case study landing page want examples and a fast way to put one customer story on its own page. The results stop at layouts and lists of well-known customer stories. This page shows four B2B case study pages built from a prompt and follows what each page does after a buyer reads it: a software company's story with one link per sales rep that emails the rep when a prospect opens it, an IT provider's page that leads with the story from the visitor's own industry, an equipment maker's page that turns the customer's savings per compressor into an estimate for the visitor, and a draft page the featured customer approves quote by quote before it goes live. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, examples, gating, the sections a story carries, where the result goes, the call to action, customer approval, tracking which story leads to a sale, and paid traffic. Portfolio pages and agency case study indexes are siblings and stay out.
